key_insight: MECx uses a bond-informed surrogate model to efficiently search huge alloy configuration spaces and find lower-energy ordered states than direct DFT Monte Carlo within practical limits.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster discovery of ordered multi-principal element alloy structures that can tune local order, thermodynamics, and mechanical behavior for alloy design.
method: Train surrogate energy models on 100 DFT-labeled configurations stratified by bond-count space.
Use the surrogate to guide Monte Carlo exploration of ternary, quaternary, and quinary BCC alloy configuration spaces.
Validate the predicted ordered states against direct DFT-based Monte Carlo, temperature evolution, and simulated neutron diffraction.
evidence_signal: In tests on ternary through quinary BCC alloys, MECx found ordered configurations with lower energies than direct DFT-based Monte Carlo and showed transfer to selected binary subsystems without retraining.
watch_item: Performance depends on a compact but representative DFT training set, so transferability and robustness may vary outside the tested alloy chemistries and structure types.
paper_title: Bond-informed search for ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys
